description: Polyphonic low-frequency oscillator with eight shapes, a CV for the rate and the level, and a phase reset

params.text: Chooses the waveform: Sine, Triangle, Square, Pulse, Ramp, Saw, Sample & hold or Warped
Sets the rate, -10 to 10 octaves, the hover text reading the result in hertz
Sets the output level, 0V to 5V either side of zero in bipolar mode
Restarts the waveform at the beginning of its cycle

inputs.text: Added to the Freq knob at one octave per volt
Added to the Amp knob one volt for one volt, the total clamped to 10V
A rise of more than half a volt from the last sample restarts the waveform at the beginning of its cycle

outputs.text: The waveform, centred on 0V in bipolar mode or running from 0V upwards in unipolar mode

notes: the channel count of the output is the largest of the three input jacks, so with nothing patched it is a single channel
the reset jack looks for a step of more than half a volt rather than a fixed threshold, so a slowly rising voltage will not restart the cycle
menu: Reduce internal sample rate: 1x to 1024x — runs the oscillator at a fraction of the sample rate, which costs much less processor time and is harmless on slow shapes
Bipolar — switches between a waveform centred on 0V and one running from 0V up to twice the Amp setting

inputs.0:
1V per octave · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.1:
±10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
